jurisdiction.title: County
jurisdiction.description: Which county to ask. There is no auto-detection: resolving a county from an address is a separate problem, and guessing it wrong returns a confident answer about the wrong property. Each county is reached a completely different way, which affects how fast the answer comes and how fresh it is.
enumTitles: San Diego County, CA (live, about 1.5 s, no freshness signal)
Duval County, FL (live, about 2 s by parcel id, values are one assessment year behind)
Travis County, TX (not implemented yet, no live endpoint exists)

lookupBy.title: Look up by
lookupBy.description: Whether the query is a parcel identifier or a street address. State it explicitly. It is never inferred from the shape of the string, because parcel identifiers have no common format and some of them look like house numbers.

query.title: Parcel identifier or address
query.description:
The parcel identifier or the street address.

There is no national parcel identifier and no per-state one either, so this field cannot be validated beyond 'not empty'. Real examples, one per county: San Diego 3532803300 (ten digits), Duval 0991354355R (ten digits and a letter), Cook 29352110190000 (fourteen digits), Travis 107422 (six digits). Two counties in the same state do not necessarily agree: another Florida county writes 07702-000-000.

For an address, give as much as you have, for example '7519 Caravaca Ct, Jacksonville, FL 32244'. An address that names a building rather than a single parcel, such as a condominium tower, returns every unit and says so in the flags.

maxResults.title: Maximum records
maxResults.description: How many parcels to return at most. Address lookups are ambiguous by nature: a house number and a street name are not unique across a county of a million parcels, and one condominium address can be hundreds of parcels. When more matched than were returned, the record says so in result_set and flags results_truncated.
